newsitem.title: CHINA: Unilever plans $100 mln China investment.
newsitem.headline: Unilever plans $100 mln China investment.

text.p: Unilever plans to invest at least $100 million more in China in the next few years to expand production and increase training for Chinese employees, the Xinhua news agency quoted chairman Morris Tabaksblal as saying.

Since 1986, Unilever has invested $350 million in setting up 11 joint ventures and two independent businesses in China and its products include more than 10 brands of washing powder, cosmetics and toothpaste, it quoted him as saying in an overnight report.
Unilever's sales volume in China was expected to surpass 5.0 billion yuan this year, Tabaksblal was quoted as saying in an interview in Shanghai.
Unilever regarded Shanghai as the base for its business operations in China because of the city's special status in China's rapid economic expansion and great potential, he said.
It was a peak time to invest in China, he said. Unilever will not only boost production and marketing, but is setting up a research centre for basic chemical engineering, he said.
